content.title: Risk stratification and assessment in acute pulmonary embolism (PE)
content.abbreviations: PE = pulmonary embolism; PESI = Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index; RV = right ventricle; sPESI = simplified Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index.

legend.c: Transthoracic echocardiography or computed tomography pulmonary angiography.

content.recommendations_summary: Initial risk stratification of suspected or confirmed PE should be based on presence of haemodynamic instability to identify patients at high risk of early mortality. In patients without haemodynamic instability, further stratification of patients with acute PE into intermediate- and low-risk categories is recommended. Use of clinical prediction rules integrating PE severity and comorbidity, preferably the PESI or sPESI, should be considered for risk assessment in the acute phase. Assessment of the RV by imaging methods or laboratory biomarkers should be considered, even in the presence of a low PESI or a negative sPESI. In patients without haemodynamic instability, validated scores combining clinical, imaging, and laboratory PE-related prognostic factors may be considered to further stratify severity of the acute PE episode.
content.diagnostic_tests: Transthoracic echocardiography or computed tomography pulmonary angiography recommended for RV assessment/diagnosis as appropriate.
content.laboratory_biomarkers: Cardiac troponins or natriuretic peptides suggested as laboratory biomarkers for risk assessment/prognosis in PE.
content.notes: Table(s) in the image present class and level of evidence for the listed recommendations (classes I, IIa, IIb etc.; levels B, C shown).
